topic: Show an in-order traversal of a binary search tree
title: In-Order Traversal, Step by Step

scenes.narration: A traversal visits every node of a tree exactly once. In order means: first the whole left subtree, then the node itself, then the right subtree. On a binary search tree that lists the values from smallest to largest.
scenes.caption: Left, node, right

scenes.narration: From 8 we go left to 3, then left again to 1. It has no left child, so 1 is visited first.
scenes.caption: visit 1

scenes.narration: The left subtree of 3 is done, so now we visit 3 itself, before going to its right side.
scenes.caption: visit 3

scenes.narration: Next comes the right subtree of 3, which is just the node 6. That finishes everything on the left of 8.
scenes.caption: visit 6

scenes.narration: With the whole left side done, we visit 8. Notice the order so far: 1, 3, 6, 8, already sorted.
scenes.caption: visit 8

scenes.narration: Now the right subtree of 8. Its smallest node is 10, which has no left child, so 10 is next.
scenes.caption: visit 10

scenes.narration: Last comes 14, the right child of 10. Every node was visited once, in increasing order.
scenes.caption: visit 14

scenes.narration: In-order traversal gave us 1, 3, 6, 8, 10 and 14. Pre-order and post-order use the same walk but visit the node before or after its children.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: In-order: left subtree, node, right subtree
On a BST it lists values in sorted order
Every node is visited once: O(n)

quiz.question: Insert 5, 3, 8, 2 and 4 into a BST. A pre-order traversal visits three nodes. Which ones, in order?
quiz.explanation: Pre-order visits a node before its children: 5, then its left child 3, then 2.

quiz.question: Insert 5, 3, 8, 2 and 4 into a BST. What is its full post-order traversal?
quiz.explanation: Post-order visits both children first, so the root 5 comes last.
